name: Early Experience

construction.unit: one training example built from the agent's own step off an expert state: (state, alternative action) → observed next state (IWM), or state → reflection + expert action (SR)
construction.kept_as: IWM: next-state text as observed (summarised by the model on WebShop, SearchQA and WebArena); SR: LLM-written reflection plus the expert action
construction.processing: at each expert state the initial policy proposes K non-expert actions (or they are sampled from the admissible list); each is executed and its next state recorded; for SR an LLM compares expert and alternative outcomes and explains the expert choice
construction.writer: SFT of the policy LLM (Llama-3.2-3B, Qwen-2.5-7B, Llama-3.1-8B; LoRA for 70B); reflections written by the same policy model (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct for all models on TravelPlanner)

organization.structure: parametric: everything is trained into the policy's weights; no external store
organization.stores: rollout set D_rollout and reflection set D_refl exist only as training data

management.operations: IWM: one epoch of next-state prediction, then imitation on expert data with the remaining step budget; SR: reflection data mixed with expert data in one SFT run
management.conflicts: SR drops reflections whose concluded action is not the expert action (BFCLv3, WebArena); Tau-Bench drops a few 'low-quality' reflections without saying by what test

retrieval.candidates: no retrieval: the policy reads only the current state

use.context: current task and state only; learned dynamics and reflections act through the weights
use.reasoning: one action per step; SR-trained models write a reflection before the action

classify.note: Parametric memory: the agent's own off-expert experience is distilled into the policy by SFT before deployment, and nothing is stored or looked up at test time. 'Consolidate' stands for this offline distillation.

stages.ingestion: Starts from expert demonstrations split into (state, expert action) pairs, 1,395 to 21,031 per environment (App. C).
stages.construction: At each expert state the initial policy proposes K alternative actions (or they are drawn from the admissible list); each is executed and the resulting next state is recorded as (state, action, next state). For SR, an LLM is shown the expert action, its outcome and the alternatives with their outcomes, and writes a reflection explaining the expert choice.
stages.answer: The fine-tuned policy acts from the current state alone; an SR-trained policy writes its reasoning, then the action.
stages.learning: IWM trains next-state prediction for one epoch, then imitation on expert data within the same step budget as the IL baseline; SR trains on reflection + expert action mixed with expert data. Checkpoints can then start GRPO where a reward exists.

summary: Turns the agent's own non-expert actions at expert states into reward-free supervision (predicting the next state, or reflecting on why the expert action was better) and trains it into the policy, as a bridge between imitation learning and RL.
notes: VENUE: ICML 2026 main (the PDF v3 carries the PMLR 306 ICML header; OpenReview N3dXUHY5dD lists 'ICML 2026 regular'). CODE: the paper links no code. OSU-NLP-Group/EarlyExperience (author group, created 2026-06, after the paper) ships only method notes, per-env READMEs and a Hugging Face dataset, with a unified training setup and different numbers; it is recorded as a data/notes release, not the evaluation code. MEMORY FRAMING: there is no retrieval-time memory; the 'memory' is the agent's own interaction experience written into the weights. RESULTS: Table 1 'SearchQA (F1)' equals the Musique column of Table 7, so those rows are stored under musique. Table 7 also covers Gemma-3-4B, which is absent from Table 1.

sources.code_note: No code is linked in the paper. The authors' group later released method notes, per-environment READMEs and SFT data (commit 3810f05e, 2026-07-08). The repo contains no training or evaluation code, uses a unified training setup, and its README reports numbers that differ from the paper, so every mechanism detail below comes from the paper.

headline: No reward is used: the only new signal is the next state the environment returns after the agent's own non-expert action.
Nothing is retrieved at test time. The experience reaches the agent only through SFT of its weights.
IWM does not add training steps: one epoch of next-state prediction comes out of the imitation budget.

discussion.takeaway: An agent can learn from the outcomes of its own non-expert actions without any reward, either by predicting those outcomes or by explaining why the expert's choice was better. Both beat imitation learning in all eight environments and give a better starting point for RL.

claims.claim: Early experience improves over imitation learning in every setting.
claims.evidence: Table 1: 8 benchmarks × 3 models; IWM +0.9 to +18.4, SR +0.6 to +15.0 points over IL (§5.2).
Table 2: ALFWorld OOD IWM +14.8 (Llama-3.1-8B); BFCLv3 OOD SR +8.5 (3B); SearchQA OOD +2.2 to +4.9 (§5.3).

claims.claim: It is a better starting point for RL.
claims.evidence: Fig. 3, Tables 4, 5, 7: after identical GRPO, e.g. ALFWorld 99.2 (SR) vs 92.2 (IL) for 3B; WebShop 92.2 (IWM) vs 82.0 (IL) (§5.4).
WebShop with 1/8 and ALFWorld with 1/2 of the demonstrations already beat IL on all of them (Fig. 4a, §6.1).

claims.claim: Grounded reflections beat ungrounded ones and preference training.
claims.evidence: Table 3: STaR-style rationales drop WebShop from 47.3 to 25.0; DPO reaches 53.1 but collapses; IWM 58.6, SR 58.2 (§6.3).

limits: The paper has no limitations section; the impact statement notes that needing less data also lowers the barrier to training agents for malicious use.
Open action spaces (free-form search queries in SearchQA, fine-grained web actions in WebArena) are named the hardest regime (§5.2).
reading: Table 1's 'SearchQA (F1)' numbers are the Musique column of Table 7, while Figure 3 uses the four-dataset average; the two are different measures under one name.
Table 2's SearchQA OOD values are not the mean of the other three Table 7 columns, and the paper does not say how they are formed.

Expert data differ by environment: optimal walkthroughs (ALFWorld, ScienceWorld), human or leaderboard-agent trajectories (WebShop, WebArena), and LLM-synthesised trajectories filtered by success (Tau-Bench, SearchQA, BFCLv3, TravelPlanner).

The number of alternatives, how they are drawn (policy samples vs uniform from the admissible list) and whether next states are summarised all change per environment, so the effect of each choice is only tested for K (Fig. 4b, two environments).
SR on TravelPlanner uses reflections written by Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct for all three trained models, so the 3B and Qwen results there are partly distillation from a different model.
Absolute scores stay low on WebArena-Lite: at most 8.5% success for the 3B-8B models, so gains of 1.2-3.6 points there rest on a 165-task set.

abstract.text: Most language agents are trained by imitating expert demonstrations, which cover few situations, while RL needs rewards that many environments do not provide. This paper proposes 'early experience': at states from expert trajectories the agent tries its own alternative actions and records what happens, using those future states as supervision with no reward. Two methods use this data: implicit world modeling, which trains the policy to predict next states, and self-reflection, which trains it to explain why the expert action beats the alternatives before acting. Across eight environments and several model families both improve over imitation learning, generalise better out of domain, and give stronger starting points for later RL.
